name: ripple-consumers-updated
body:
The ripple consumers must stay in sync with the new surface (SPEC §6):
- Suite tools `opencode-suite/tools/*.ts` (embedded in `src/main.rs` via `include_str!`): `apg_plan_init.ts` → a plan-`add` tool; `apg_plan_add.ts` must treat `kind` as optional (= the plan itself); new `apg_node`/`apg_edge` update/rm variants; new plan update/rm tools; retire `apg_plan_link.ts`.
- Distributed agent prompts `opencode-suite/agents/*.md` (plan-writer, spec-writer, codebase-navigator) reference `apg plan init` / `apg_plan_init` / `apg_plan_link` — update to the new verbs.
- Root `AGENTS.md` CLI reference block lists `apg plan <sub> … init/add/link/…` — update to `add/update/rm/…`.
Acceptance: no shipped tool/agent/AGENTS.md text names the retired verbs; the renamed/new tools dispatch the new CLI surface. NOTE: these consumers' solution coverage anchors to the embedding/install Rust (`apg.main` / `apg.install_suite` / `apg.cmd_init`) because the DELIVERED artifact is the embedded constant — the `include_str!` text compiled into the binary and written to the user-level suite by `apg.install_suite` — NOT because the source files are unscannable. This is a delivery-semantics choice, mirroring `solution.note.markdown-anchoring` / `solution.note.coordinator-feedback-routing`. The `opencode-suite/tools/*.ts` files are in fact ALREADY scanned File nodes with `code_type src` (e.g. `opencode-suite/tools/apg_review_action.ts`), and under the markdown frontend this spec adds (`requirements.requirement.markdown-frontend`) `opencode-suite/agents/*.md` and AGENTS.md become scanned File/Struct section nodes (FQN = the absolute path). Both are legitimate `implemented-by` targets: the code-FQN universe is the Module/Struct/Function/File records with no `status` set (src/main.rs:1342-1364) and `classify_code_ref` grades Real/Pending/Drift off that universe independent of file extension (src/layers.rs:1295-1329). The anchor deliberately stays on the embedding/install Rust for delivery semantics.
